ns2:course.label: Archival Arrangement and Description
ns2:course.description: Provides seminar discussions and a hands-on processing experience that applies current theories and practices utilized to solve the most common problems that are encountered by today's archivists and curators when arranging and describing historical records, archives, manuscripts, and artifacts. Issues of intellectual and physical arrangement, description, and access are addressed. 2 graduate hours. No professional credit.
ns2:course.sectionDeptRestriction: Restricted to students in the Information Sciences department.
